rows.headWhy: The yellow iris with a hard vertical slit pupil is the one genuinely species-specific mark in this batch — you could not slot this head onto any other animal here unnoticed. But that is the eye alone doing the work. The skull under it is the same generic cone-muzzle ovoid as the rest, and it is sabotaged by a large grey-rimmed pink-centred disc plastered above and behind the eye (the ear) that is bigger than the eye and reads as a second, larger eye, giving the face a lemur/seal look.
rows.defect: (1) FEET: the leg zoom is unambiguous — smooth cylinders ending in two grey cloven toe caps. This is a CAT and it has hooves. No paw, no toe pads, no broad snowshoe foot. (2) LEGS are straight dowels with no elbow, no hock, no crouch; the reference calls for short stout legs and big paws and delivers ungulate stilts. (3) TAIL: instead of the enormously long thick ropy tail (the single most identifiable snow leopard feature) there is a short pale stub fringed with a fan of black bristles — the same bristle-fan tail the Hyena has. (4) Rosettes are rendered as solid black blobs and clusters, not open rings with a pale centre. (5) The ear disc is a flat circle stamped on the skull surface with no thickness or attachment.
rows.fix: Route this species to the paw foot: broad rounded pad with four toe bumps, thick low-set limbs with a visible elbow and hock break. Rebuild the tail as a single thick tube of constant diameter, length >= head+body, curving up and out — kill the bristle fan primitive entirely for felids. Convert the spot marks to annuli: dark ring with the base coat showing through the centre, only the head and legs getting solid dots. Re-seat the ear as a small rounded triangle rising from the skull outline rather than a disc drawn on the cheek.

rows.readsAs: A hornless grey ram, or a very large shaggy rat
rows.headWhy: This is the Sloth Bear's head with the ears changed from pointed leaves to a flat dark disc. Same long tapering snout, same nose bead, same tiny white-ringed eye, same curved mouth line. Swapping the two would go unnoticed. Worse, the species' ONE naming feature — the cream rings around the eyes — is not present at all; the pale ring visible at the eye is the batch-standard white sclera donut, which every animal here has, so the head carries zero species information.
rows.defect: (1) No spectacle markings. The face is uniform dark brown with nothing around the eye. (2) FEET are the same dark cloven caps with vestigial white claw slivers — not a bear's flat plantigrade sole. (3) The muzzle is long and tapered where the reference calls for a short rounded face with a heavy muzzle; the profile is more rodent than ursine. (4) The ear is a flat dark circle drawn on the side of the cranium with a separate small square tab behind it — two conflicting ear objects on one head. (5) Body mass is wrong for a bear: barrel torso on thin straight legs with no shoulder hump and no rump bulk.
rows.fix: Paint the spectacles: two cream rings (or arcs) around the eye extending down the cheek, high value contrast against the near-black coat. Shorten the muzzle to ~0.2 of head length and blunt the front so the profile is a rounded box. Give it the plantigrade sole foot — a wide flat pad the full length of the lower limb with five short dark claws at the front. Resolve the double ear into one small rounded ear with thickness, attached at the skull outline. Thicken the limbs and add shoulder/haunch mass so the standing pose reads heavy.

rows.readsAs: A spotted pony or an appaloosa donkey
rows.headWhy: The distinguishing element is a dark triangle sitting on top of the skull like a folded paper cone — a bolt-on, not skull architecture, and it is the wrong ear anyway (spotted hyenas have big ROUNDED ears, per the reference row). Remove it and what remains is the same ovoid cranium, same long tapering cone muzzle with a nose bead, same white-donut eye that the Sloth, Stoat and both bears wear. The head is also far too small and too finely tapered to read as the heaviest jaws in the carnivore world.
rows.defect: (1) FEET: cloven hooves again — two dark toe caps on smooth cylindrical legs. A hyena needs blunt non-retractile claws on a compact dog-like paw. (2) The signature sloping topline is missing: in the body crop the back is nearly level, with only a slight rise toward the shoulder, and the hips are as tall as the withers. (3) The neck is a thin tube where the reference demands a massive thick neck. (4) TAIL is the same black bristle-fan as the Snow Leopard's — hyena tails are a short dark tufted whip, not a spread fan. (5) The ears are a single midline triangle rather than two round ears on the sides of the skull. (6) The muzzle tapers to a point; there is no blocky jaw depth or masseter bulk.
rows.fix: Raise the shoulder attachment ~15% of body height above the hip attachment and run the spine as a single straight downward diagonal from withers to rump — that one line is the whole species. Thicken the neck to at least 0.8 of head depth and merge it into the shoulder mass. Swap cloven feet for the dog-paw primitive. Deepen the muzzle to a blunt wedge with a visible jaw angle under the eye. Replace the crest triangle with two large rounded ears placed on the sides of the crown. Convert the bristle-fan tail to a short tapering tube with a dark terminal tuft.

rows.readsAs: A young deer or a plain gazelle fawn — the closest to a correct read in this batch
rows.headWhy: Only the horns identify it, and they are an attachment sitting above a head that is otherwise the batch-standard cone: smooth ovoid cranium, tapering muzzle with a small nostril mark and a faint mouth line, small bead eye with the same white sclera ring. The eye is set high and close to the horn bases rather than large, dark and set far back on the side of the skull as an antelope's is; the reference asks for prominent eyes and these are the smallest in the batch. The ear is a small brown leaf hidden between the horns instead of a long lateral leaf.
rows.defect: (1) HORNS are smooth and unringed and rise as two near-vertical prongs splaying apart with only a slight inward hook — the lyre curve is missing, as are the heavy annulations that are half the identity. They also emerge too far apart, from the sides of the skull rather than the crown. (2) COAT: the animal is a single uniform cream from nose to hoof. There is no dark chocolate flank stripe, no white belly, no white rump patch, no dark facial stripe from eye to muzzle. That tricolour is the species; without it this is a generic antelope. (3) LEGS are jointless tapered dowels — no carpus, no hock angle, no cannon-bone narrowing. (4) The tail is a small brown dot. (5) Shoulder and haunch masses are soft airbrushed ovals blurred onto the torso rather than forms with an edge.
rows.fix: Rebuild the horns on a lyre path: out and back from a close-set crown origin, then a distinct forward-and-inward hook in the top third, and stamp 10-14 raised rings along the lower two thirds. Paint the three-tone coat: tan dorsal, hard-edged dark chocolate band along the lower flank from shoulder to haunch, white below it and on the rump and face, plus a dark stripe through the eye. Add a knee and hock break to the limbs and narrow the cannon. Give the ear a long lateral leaf shape clear of the horns.

rows.readsAs: A meerkat body stretched into a dachshund, standing on deer hooves
rows.headWhy: Same cone muzzle with a nose bead and same ovoid cranium as the Sloth and Hyena; the round brown disc on the crown is the same flat plastered ear circle the Spectacled Bear and Snow Leopard have, just recoloured. The eye is a large pale blue-grey orb with a round pupil, which is both oversized for the skull and the wrong colour — a stoat's eye is a small glossy black bead. Swap this head with the Sloth's and only the palette would give it away.
rows.defect: (1) FEET: cloven hooves — two dark toe caps per limb on a mustelid. It needs a small five-toed clawed paw. (2) The torso is a machined slab: the dorsal line is a perfectly straight horizontal edge running the full body length with a hard corner at each end, and the belly is equally flat. A stoat's back is a continuous flexible arch. (3) TAIL is a short stubby hook about a quarter of body length with a rust-brown tip — the reference calls for a long tail with a hard BLACK tip, and both length and colour are wrong. (4) The long neck the reference asks for is absent; the head sits directly on the shoulder. (5) Shoulder and haunch are blurred airbrushed circles stamped on the slab with no silhouette effect. (6) No white underside separating from the tan dorsal.
rows.fix: Arch the topline: sine-curve the dorsal edge so the spine humps over the shoulder, dips at the waist and rises again at the haunch, and round off the terminal corners. Extend the tail to ~40% of body length as a tapering tube and hard-cut the terminal third to pure black. Swap the foot to a small clawed paw with visible toes. Lengthen and lift the neck so the head is carried clear above the shoulder line. Shrink the eye to a small dark bead with a bright specular dot and drop the pale blue iris. Add a cream ventral field with a defined boundary along the lower flank.
